_comment: The patcher window's "?" guides. One short, plain guide for every button, tool and setting the window shows, by control key. Each guide is a list of short lines: what it does, how to use it, and what to watch out for. tests/test_how_to_use.py refuses a control without one, and a guide that is too long.

getting_started.title: Getting started
guide: This patcher makes a separate modded copy of your Virtual Families 2 folder. Your original game folder and your original saves are left alone.
1. Pick your vanilla Virtual Families 2 folder (the one holding Virtual Families 2.exe). 2. Tick the patches you want. 3. Click Dry Run, then Enable/Disable Patches.
Vanilla Virtual Families 2 saves work with the modded game. The modded game keeps its saves in its own folder, so use Back Up Saves on the Tools tab before trying a new build.

game_folder.title: Vanilla game folder
guide: The folder of your official Virtual Families 2 install: it holds Virtual Families 2.exe, Images, Sounds, Assets and the game's other program files.
Click Browse and pick it. The patcher checks it looks right before it changes anything.
Leave it empty only when you are re-configuring a modded folder you already made.

manifest.title: Patch manifest
guide: The list of patches this patcher can apply. manifest.json loads by itself when the patcher starts.
Only pick another manifest if someone gave you one.
Load Manifest Settings reads it again and redraws the patch list.

output_folders.title: Modded output folder
guide: Where the modded copy of the game goes. It is made next to your vanilla folder unless you pick another place.
Save modified folders under: the folder the new modded folder is made in. Modded output folder: an exact folder, such as one you made before.
Never pick your vanilla folder as the output folder.

backup_folder.title: Backup folder
guide: Each time you rebuild an existing modded folder, the patcher first saves a complete copy of the old one (about 230 MB).
By default each copy goes in a new dated folder under .vf2_patch_backups. Pick a folder here to put them somewhere else.
The patcher never deletes these copies: delete old ones yourself to free disk space.
These are copies of the game files. Your saves are backed up by Back Up Saves on the Tools tab.

patch_log.title: Patch log
guide: A text record of exactly what a run changed.
Leave it empty for the default place, or Browse to choose a file.
Send it along if you ask for help with a patch problem.

patch_selection.title: Choosing patches
guide: Tick the patches you want. Main Patches are the core fixes, Optional Patches add extra content, and Experimental patches are unfinished (shown in red, and off unless you tick them).
Defaults ticks the recommended set. Enable All ticks everything except Experimental. Disable All clears every tick.
Some patches need another one. Ticking one ticks what it needs, and unticking a needed patch unticks what depends on it.

family_history.title: Family History log
guide: Keeps a Family History log for each family: one dated record for each marriage, remarriage, divorce, conception, birth, death, rename and Random Event.
Each person is written with name, age, sex, head and body. Twins and triplets are marked, each death names its cause, and each marriage names the current spouse and any earlier one.
Random Events are marked Email Event or Popup Event, with the choice. Children who join or leave home, each new generation, a new family, Start Over and Evict Family are noted too.
A family you already have gets its past filled in once from its Family Tree, marked "backfilled, no date".
The log is a text file in your save folder: Virtual Families 2 Patcher\Save N\Logs\Family History.
It is on by default: Enable/Disable Patches installs it. Unticking it and rebuilding turns it off; written logs are kept.
Starting a new family or Start Over in a save slot starts that slot's log again. It is not yet tested in a running game, so back up your saves first.

expanded_flea_market.title: All 36 Flea Market goods
guide: The store's Flea Market lists all 36 of its goods at all times, as every earlier patched build did.
It is on by default. Untick it and rebuild for the original game's Flea Market: 5 goods, picked at random and picked again 6 hours of real time later.
While it is ticked all 36 goods are always in stock, even one that sold out while it was unticked.
The Towelette, the Anti-spam Software and the Rockhound Certificate can be bought again too: the first two go to the tray again, the certificate stays owned, and an owned one keeps its checkmark.

r_refreshes_store.title: R Refreshes the Store
guide: A cheat: in the store, press R (or Shift+R) to pick the store's random items again, the game's own way.
On the Clothing and Hairstyles page R picks the six outfits again. Hairstyles stay, and outfits you already bought keep their looks.
On the Flea Market page R picks 5 new goods, but only while All 36 Flea Market goods is unticked; with it ticked every good is already there, so R does nothing.
R does nothing on any other page, outside the store, or while a box is open. It never changes On Sale.
It is on by default. Unticking it and rebuilding turns it off.

fix_vanilla_game_bugs.title: Fix Vanilla Game Bugs
guide: Fixes bugs that are in the original game. It is on by default.
Menus: Start Over asks first, Pause Game: Yes works while paused, and the title screen shows the right name and buttons.
Startup: the game no longer closes by itself about 20 seconds after it starts, when LDW's server sends back a long answer. That answer is now ignored.
Outfits: each Male Outfit and Female Outfit in the tray keeps the outfit it was bought with. In the original game every outfit of a family member's sex showed, and gave, the last one bought.
Your outfits are remembered in a small file beside each save, in Virtual Families 2 Patcher Data\Outfits. The save itself is not changed.
Outfits bought before this fix look and work as they did before. The outfit fix is not yet tested in a running game.
Unticking it and clicking Enable/Disable Patches gives you the original game's behaviour back.

dry_run.title: Dry Run (Validate Only)
guide: Checks that your game folder and your patch choices work, without writing anything.
Click it before Enable/Disable Patches, especially the first time.
If it reports a problem, nothing was changed; fix what it names and run it again.

apply.title: Enable/Disable Patches
guide: Builds the modded folder from your vanilla game with exactly the patches that are ticked.
Changed your mind later? Tick or untick patches and click it again: the modded folder is rebuilt from vanilla with the new choices.
An existing modded folder is copied to the Backup folder first. You can bring it back with Restore Backup.

restore_backup.title: Restore Backup
guide: Puts back a game-folder copy the patcher made before a rebuild.
Browse to the dated backup folder and click Restore Backup. It is restored into the folder it was taken from, never into your vanilla folder.
Restore log: where to write the record of the restore (optional).
This is for game files. To bring back saved families, use Restore Saves on the Tools tab.

check_updates.title: Check for updates
guide: Opens the patcher's download page in your web browser.
Compare the build number at the top right of this window with the newest one listed there.
Back up your saves before moving to a new build.

back_up_saves.title: Back Up Saves
guide: Copies your family saves into a dated folder inside the save folder: Documents\LDW\<game>\Backups\Backup <date and time>.
It copies the game's save files and the patcher's own files too (the Virtual Families 2 Patcher Data folder, which holds the extra children).
Click it, tick the save folders to copy, click Back Up Selected. If the game is running it is paused for the copy and resumes by itself.
The game saves by itself every 2 minutes while it runs, and when you quit normally, so a backup of a running game holds your families as of the last save.
Game speed is set to Paused in the backup's family saves (your own saves are unchanged), so a restored backup opens paused and never catches up on the time since it was made.
Only a family at Normal is paused. A save at another speed, or one that cannot be read, is copied exactly as it is.
Every copied file is checked against the original. An older backup is never written over.

restore_saves.title: Restore Saves
guide: Brings back a backup made by Back Up Saves: the whole save folder, or just one family's save slot.
Quit the game first. Pick a backup (newest first), choose the whole folder or one slot, and click Restore...
You are shown exactly which files will be replaced, added or removed, and nothing changes until you say yes.
Your saves as they are now are backed up first as "Backup <date> (before restore)", so a restore can always be undone.
Delete Backup... removes a backup you no longer need.

copy_player_slot.title: Copy Player Slot
guide: Copies a family into another save slot of the same save folder, under a new name, so you can play on in two ways.
Quit the game first, from its own menu. Click Copy Player Slot..., pick the family, the slot to copy into and the new name (up to 19 characters), then Copy and Yes.
A slot with no save is empty, whatever the game's player list shows. A slot with another family is replaced only after a warning that names it.
Everything kept for the family goes too: the game's previous save, Up to 28 Children, outfit pictures, the Family History log and the Family Tree Maker's tree file.
Your saves are backed up first (Backups\Backup <date> (before copy)), and a replaced family's files are kept in Backups\Replaced by copy <date> - Save <N> - <name>.

rename_family.title: Rename Family
guide: Virtual Families 2 has no family surname: each family slot is shown under the player name typed when it was started, on the main menu and in Change Player. This changes that name.
Quit the game first, from its own menu. Click Rename Family..., pick the family, type the new name (up to 19 letters, digits, spaces and keyboard symbols), then Rename.
The game itself keeps at most 19 characters, and "NEW PLAYER" cannot be used: the game shows that for an empty slot.
Your saves are backed up first, as "Backup <date> (before rename)", so Restore Saves can undo it.

game_speed.title: Game Speed
guide: Pauses or unpauses a family in its save, the same way the game's own Pause Game option does.
Quit the game first, from its own menu. Click Game Speed..., pick the family (each shows its speed now), choose Paused or Normal, then Set Speed.
Paused works as if you paused just before the game last saved. Normal works as if you unpaused it right now, so the time it spent paused never counts.
Set Normal just before you play: like any family at normal speed, it catches up on the time the game is closed after that.
Your saves are backed up first, as "Backup <date> (before speed change)". Like every backup, its families are Paused, so restoring it brings a family back Paused.
A family at any other speed is shown but not changed here; change it in the game instead.

game_mechanics.title: Game Mechanics
guide: Shows how Virtual Families 2 works underneath: ageing, needs, illness, old age, babies, careers, money, leaving home, dating, events, weather, messes and the store.
Every time is real time at the game's normal speed. Every chance is the game's own exact chance.
Each line is marked VERIFIED-E (the game's own code was run and counted), VERIFIED-C (read from the game's own code) or UNCONFIRMED (not yet shown either way).
Click a topic's button at the top to jump to it.
It only shows text: it reads no save and changes nothing, so the game may be running.

family_tree.title: Family Tree Maker
guide: Draws a family's tree from its save: every generation's parents and children, with each face from the game.
Click Family Tree Maker..., choose the save folder and the family, then Open. Pick the game folder too, or each face shows a letter.
Click a portrait to edit its words, shape, colour and marks. Save keeps your tree for next time; Export as Picture saves a PNG or JPG.
The game forgets a spouse who died with no children once a new spouse marries in, and a divorced spouse. The tree remembers them, if it was opened while they were still in the save.
With the Family History log, twins and triplets, causes of death and earlier marriages show too. Without it the tree says what is not known.
Your saves are only read, never changed.

picture_maker.title: Picture Maker
guide: Draws the game's pictures exactly as the game draws them, saved as PNGs with a clear background.
From my save: pick the save folder and family. Everyone at home can be drawn in the house, on the Details screen, an event screen or the Family Tree; others in the Family Tree.
Make your own: pick the sex, age, head, outfit and how it is drawn. Children are smaller and heads turn old at 45, as in the game.
Carrying (in the house): any item a family member can hold, even ones the game never shows (marked).
All game pictures: every sprite, frame, button, bar and background, the unused ones and the patcher's too. Search, then Save all shown (a folder per category).
Pick the game folder: the pictures come from it. Patched look off shows the original game's outfits.
Save PNG: game size, 2x or 4x (crisp), or your own size (smooth). Saves and game folders are only read.

how_to_use.title: How to Use guide
guide: Opens the full guide: every button and tool in this patcher, one short page each.
Pick a topic on the left to read it.
Every "?" button in the window opens the page for the control beside it.
